steps.text: Grate tomatoes into a bowl using a box grater; discard tomato skins.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in rice and cook, stirring often, until rice is lightly toasted, about 3 more minutes. Stir in grated tomato, chicken broth, and tomato sauce; bring mixture to a boil.
Stir in jalapeño pepper, cilantro, and salt; reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet and simmer until liquid has been absorbed, about 15 minutes. Do not lift the cover while rice is cooking.
Turn off the heat; let rice stand, covered, for 8 minutes. Fluff with a fork before transferring rice to a serving dish.

raw_recipe.headline: Arroz Rojo (Mexican Red Rice)
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican red rice with garlic and jalapeño is a deliciously savory tomato-flavored rice that makes an authentic side dish for Mexican meals.

review.reviewBody: This was very good and very easy. I made enough for 45 people and everyone enjoyed it. My only change - My altered servings called for many many Roma tomatoes, peeled. I drained a #10 can of diced tomatoes and it worked perfectly.

I haven’t made Mexican rice in awhile, so maybe my memory is foggy, but I’m not sure I’ve ever made a Mexican rice recipe quite this good. Rather than trying to grate a tomato, I simply blanched it which made the peel come off easily, then just chopped it up very fine. Scaling this down to two servings meant I had to improvise on the tomato sauce – I wasn’t about to open a can for a mere tablespoon or two. For those who might find themselves in the same situation, I used half the measurement in tomato paste and water instead and it obviously worked out great because this was simply delicious. Worth seriously considering for your go-to Mexican rice side dish.

I tried making it following the recipe, but it didn't have enough liquid to get my rice soft. I ended up adding a can of tomatoes and a lot more water to get it to cook properly. I used brown rice instead of white, so maybe that was why.
The taste was good. I didn't use cilantro because I'm one of those people who think it tastes like soap.

This is definitely the best Mexican style rice I've made to date! It was very simple and quick. Although, I thought peeling and grating the tomatoes was ridiculous, I grated my fingers more than I grated the tomatoes - so next time I'm just going to peel them with my hand peeler and pulse them in a food processor until they are chopped very fine.

Really good. Substituted the Grated tomatoes with cherry tomatoes, and canned + drained green chiles for the jalapeno. Topped with 
some avocado, lime juice, and added some marinated chicken as the main course

Very, very good! I added some cumin in for extra flavor, and instead of using roma tomatoes and tomato sauce, I used a can of diced tomatoes. I almost thought I would have to much liquid, but it turned out great! Also I used Uncle Ben's Original whit rice and let it simmer for 20 minutes, so probably for the time use whatever the rice you're using says. Maybe add taco beef next time to make it a mea. :)

We really enjoyed this rice. I did make changes though. In order to make it a one pot meal, I added a pound of browned hamburger. No fresh tomatoes, so I used a can of diced tomatoes and added some green pepper which I cooked with the onion. My rice needed to cook a little longer than 15 minutes, I think 18 would probably be good.

i used a can of fire roasted tomatoes in place of the Roma tomatoes! Family LOVED it
,

Super, super simple to make and, if you use vegetable broth instead of the chicken, completely vegetarian. I'm not sure it was worth grating Roma tomatoes if you don't keep them on hand, I could have chopped up regular ones, but the color was fun. Just remember, a pepper goes a long way. Be sure you are comfortable with how much you are putting in, particularly if you are serving this to company.

Really liked. Made exactly as written and made to pair with a beef barbacoa recipe from this site. I think the shredding of the Roma tomatoes is a bit unnecessary unless you have a diner who is vehemently opposed to them. I did it but I think if you/your guests like tomatoes, chopping them or adding a can of Rotel works just as well. Could use a little more seasoning like cumin or cayenne but overall, really good take on Spanish or Mexican rice. It’s super easy and allows you to finish other aspects of your meal while this is simmering on the stove. Would make again. Thanks Paulette!

This was the first time I tried making Mexican rice. I wanted rice to go with birria (also the first time making that!). I followed the recipe as is except I used a cored and seeded serrano pepper instead of a japaleno. It was a little spicy but really good.
I changed the jalapeño for poblanos. I added chicken. I cooked the onions with a red pepper. Added a little turmeric, cummin, and a little black pepper.
Great way to make it from scratch.
Loved this! Finally a Mexican rice that is flavorful! I used can crushed tomatoes drained, and doubled the recipe for our Mexican themed dinner- it was a HUGE success!❤️
Added 1 can of SW Chilli Beans in Zesty tomato sauce and substituted 1 can Petite Diced Tomatoes instead of fresh tomatoes and tomato sauce,

This was an easy, yummy recipe. I’d never done homemade Spanish or Mexican rice. It was a hit in my house. To save time and a little work, I used a 1/2 cup of canned diced tomatoes instead of fresh grated. I left out the jalapeño because of my toddler, but the tomatoes I used were fire roasted with green chilies and added some great flavor. I’ll definitely be making this again!
So simple & flavorful! I add chicken Knorr seating for the salt& i barely add about half a tablespoon. Other recipes i need to add so much seasoning! Will be sharing this with everyone! Thank you!
It was good and pretty easy. I've never grated tomato before, next time I would probably just use canned tomatoes as grating made a bit of a mess.
Really good as a side dish but needs a little extra spice as a main dish.
I have been making this rice for years whenever it is Mexican night. It is excellent. It is better if you make your own broth but the others will do. One warning: you will get hooked on this!
